name: Khanate
label: Hydra Head
lede: Four men from OLD, Burning Witch, Sunn O))) and Blind Idiot God play at a crawl in Jersey City, and Alan Dubin's shriek turns it into New York's most punishing band.

eras.title: Four men, one Jersey City rehearsal room
eras.text: Two OLD veterans, a Seattle doom guitarist relocated to New York, and a jazz-trained drummer start improvising at absurd volume and glacial speed. By the end of 2001 they have a debut on Southern Lord Records built from edited jams.

years.src: CLRVYNT oral history · The Quietus · Dead End Follies
years.h: Plotkin meets O'Malley at an Isis show at Brownies
years.p: [[James Plotkin|d5fc2614-ce13-4d96-8e33-c855cd8eb3f3]] introduces [[Stephen O'Malley|d2db31eb-4469-4e8d-8ed2-b3c1bfff0c17]] to his old bandmate [[Alan Dubin|482f7f7b-9ccf-440f-9e84-f64da9e7351f]] and to drummer [[Tim Wyskida|321b3f6e-b1e7-4d07-9bdd-324d8caf76d0]], and the four start rehearsing in Wyskida's Jersey City space.
years.xp:
Plotkin and Dubin had met in New Jersey as teenagers and made grindcore together in [[OLD|2a7e17f0-dc67-4902-ad4b-20bd986e847b]]. O'Malley, previously of [[Burning Witch|e5d4491d-1496-4efa-a5b9-e7be001b9f6a]] and by then a co-founder of [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]], had moved to New York and was working a Midtown advertising job. Wyskida, of [[Blind Idiot God|3165e9a0-c313-47ac-ab99-f36834365e9b]], came up through jazz training.

The band's own account has the first meeting at an Isis show at the East Village club Brownies, while Dubin dates the meeting to 2000. Stephen O'Malley later told The Quietus he first weighed the name Ögedi, after Genghis Khan's son, before settling on Khanate.

years.h: The tektonikdoom CDR: twenty copies on yellow vellum
years.p: Before any label deal, the band pressed a 20-copy CDR demo called tektonikdoom.

years.h: Khanate: five tracks, 56 minutes, Southern Lord SUNN14
years.p: Recorded in Wyskida's rehearsal space on a digital 8-track, then assembled by Plotkin in Cubase from riffs and edited improvisations. Opens with the 13-minute "Pieces of Quiet" and ends on "No Joy".
years.xp:
O'Malley recalls using anything in the room as a microphone, with foam and a speaker cabinet wrapped around the computer so the volume wouldn't crash it. Songs such as "Skin Coat" and "Under Rotting Sky" were written first; much of the rest was cut together from jams.

Southern Lord Records issued it as SUNN14. Julian Cope reviewed it in March 2002 and called it an "orchestrated root-canal".

eras.title: The $666 record
eras.text: A live radio set, a borrowed 16-track and a tiny budget produce the record most fans point to first. Khanate's Sunset Park sessions are also where Dubin's vocals start costing him his breath.

years.h: Live WFMU 91.1: the band on New Jersey radio
years.p: A live set for freeform station WFMU became one of Khanate's first live documents.

years.cap: The Brooklyn loft where Things Viral took shape
years.h: Things Viral: recorded above a tire shop on a $666 budget
years.p: [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]] of Southern Lord Records gave the band $666, which bought a few microphones; a Roland 16-track came on loan from [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] of Hydra Head Records.
years.xp:
The sessions took place in Andy Hawkins' loft in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, above a tire shop. Hawkins plays in [[Blind Idiot God|3165e9a0-c313-47ac-ab99-f36834365e9b]] with Wyskida. O'Malley switched from a Les Paul Custom to a Travis Bean guitar around this time and says the whole band changed once it arrived.

The Quietus reports Dubin would run out of breath and pass out from screaming during sessions, and recorded in a closet at SAR Studios. O'Malley remembers the loft scene as devoted but desperate, with real tension between the four.

years.h: Things Viral: four tracks, 59 minutes, Southern Lord
years.p: Opens with the 19-minute "Commuted" and closes with "Too Close Enough to Touch". Pitchfork gave it 8.2, and a video was made for "Dead".
years.xp: James Plotkin produced, recorded and mixed it, and plays bass plus keyboards and synths. It came out as a European digipack, a U.S. jewelcase CD, and a 1,000-copy gatefold LP on Load Records. Plotkin describes it as an album about space and decay.

years.p: Southern Lord follows the album with a remix EP built around the debut's closing track "No Joy".

eras.title: Capture, release, quit
eras.text: Touring hard, especially in Europe, the band moves from edited jams to songs built in the rehearsal room. That shift, plus schedules and a lot of personal friction, ends it in the autumn of 2006.

years.h: Live releases pile up: a 230-copy DVD and a Stockholm split
years.p: Let Loose the Lambs, a limited tour DVD (230 copies), and KHNT vs. Stockholm both appear in 2004 as the band tours behind Things Viral.
years.xp: Things Viral drew a particularly strong reception in Europe, and audiences there went well beyond the usual metal crowd, according to Plotkin and O'Malley in the CLRVYNT oral history. O'Malley says the shows were about the performance itself, since anything could go wrong at that tempo.

years.h: Capture & Release: two tracks, 43 minutes, Hydra Head
years.p: "Capture" runs 18 minutes and "Release" 25, on Hydra Head Records (HH666-87).
years.xp:
Recorded at Seizures Palace in Brooklyn with engineer [[Martin Bisi|cc9c5e4f-72dc-4525-8abd-63ba3d2b1a5b]], it was the band's first album on tape, and tracking finished on day three of four booked days. The songs were worked out together in rehearsal rather than assembled on a computer. O'Malley and Wyskida drove the writing, and Plotkin says he felt sidelined.

Pitchfork gave it 7.7. Plotkin says it is about density where Things Viral was about space.

years.h: Atlanta, the Drunken Unicorn, 20 to 30 people
years.p: On the fall 2005 tour behind Capture & Release the band plays Atlanta's Drunken Unicorn to a small crowd, a show covered in the CLRVYNT oral history.

years.h: Dead/Live Aktions DVD and a 500-copy live album
years.p: The band adds a DVD, Dead/Live Aktions, and a limited live album, It's Cold When Birds Fall from the Sky (500 copies).

years.big: A band on hiatus, a tour on the calendar
q: everyone was a total dick in their own individual way
years.h: Sunn O))) tours, Khanate stalls, Plotkin leaves
years.p: After a six-week Sunn O))) run, Stephen O'Malley asks for a break, then Sunn O))) takes a Celtic Frost support tour.
years.xp:
On September 24, 2006, James Plotkin announced he was leaving Khanate, citing a lack of commitment from certain members. In a November 17 follow-up he pointed to Alan Dubin's TV commercial editing job as an obstacle to rehearsing, recording and touring, and said O'Malley's casual attitude compounded it.

O'Malley says he returned from that spring 2006 tour with his personal life a mess and asked for time off. Wyskida told CLRVYNT that O'Malley putting Sunn O))) first, along with tension over the creative process and money, ended the band.

eras.title: Offshoots, a last record, and a reunion that didn't happen
eras.text: The members scatter into other groups, then a fourth album assembled from unused tape appears in 2009. Festival offers arrive; nobody bites.

years.p: [[James Plotkin|d5fc2614-ce13-4d96-8e33-c855cd8eb3f3]] and [[Tim Wyskida|321b3f6e-b1e7-4d07-9bdd-324d8caf76d0]] form [[Khlyst|dbae5f36-c626-426b-bb6b-d4de8289c2a3]] and [[Jodis|6064aabc-7cbf-473c-98d7-ba1eb17afa21]] (with [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]]), [[Alan Dubin|482f7f7b-9ccf-440f-9e84-f64da9e7351f]] starts [[Gnaw|cd349e0b-5b88-4e70-8f41-7582ffdbe723]], and [[Stephen O'Malley|d2db31eb-4469-4e8d-8ed2-b3c1bfff0c17]] keeps [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]] going and moves to Paris.

years.h: Clean Hands Go Foul: the posthumous fourth album
years.p: Four tracks and 60 minutes on Hydra Head Records, the last is nearly 33 minutes long. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the recording to sessions in 2005, 2006 and 2008 at Seizures Palace. Wyskida told CLRVYNT it came from leftover tape from the Capture & Release session, mostly improvisations with little editing, which Plotkin rediscovered years later and Dubin sang over.

years.p: Promoters come calling after Clean Hands Go Foul, but the talks fall through. O'Malley says writing riffs got hard after Khanate.
years.xp: The CLRVYNT oral history lists logistics and unwanted afternoon open-air slots among the reasons. Wyskida said a return was unlikely, though not impossible.

years.h: A Drag City compilation session puts them back in a room
years.p: The band records for a Drag City compilation, and Wyskida says they realized they wanted to do more together.

years.h: Hydra Head reissues Things Viral on silver double LP
years.p: A limited 500-copy deluxe gatefold 2xLP on silver vinyl appears in 2016.

eras.title: To Be Cruel
eras.text: The band quietly gets back to work, then drops a surprise album in 2023 on Sacred Bones.

years.p: Khanate begins writing again in between other projects, and does not announce it for years.

years.cap: To Be Cruel, Sacred Bones Records, 2023
years.h: To Be Cruel arrives with no warning, 14 years on
years.p: Khanate's first album since 2009 drops digitally on Sacred Bones Records on May 19, with physical copies on June 30.
years.xp: It was recorded at Orgone studio in Woburn, England, which O'Malley describes as a WWII radio building that broadcast fake German radio into occupied France. Dubin described the album as portraying a self-immolating destiny that perhaps ironically blames outside entities. Digital reissues of the four earlier albums were announced at the same time, with physical reissues to follow.
